0.0.n: その refers back to the previously described events, and 後 indicates a later time.

0.2.n: This is the name of one of the three clans.

0.4.n: This is the name of one of the three clans.

0.6.n: This is the name of one of the three clans.

0.7.n: Links the list of names to the following description as three clans.

0.8.n: Uses つ, a general counting ending, to count the clans.

0.9.n: Connects the quantity ３つ to the noun 氏族.

0.10.n: Refers to groups connected by family lineage, here the three named ruling families.

0.11.n: Marks the three clans as the topic; what they do follows in the next line.

1.0.n: Before の家, this distributes the destination among the different families.

1.1.n: Links それぞれ to 家, indicating each separate family.

1.2.n: Here 家 means a family or household, not a physical house.

1.3.n: Marks the family a daughter joins through marriage.

1.4.n: Before の娘, this indicates daughters belonging to the respective clans.

1.5.n: Links それぞれ to 娘, showing whose daughters are involved.

1.6.n: Japanese nouns do not require plural endings; the context supplies the plural here.

1.7.n: Marks the daughters as the people being married off.

1.8.n: The causing form of 嫁ぐ shows the clans arranging for their daughters to marry into other families.

1.9.n: Turns the preceding action into a noun-like phrase so it can combine with で.

1.10.n: Marks the marriage arrangements as the means of forming the alliance.

1.12.n: Pairs with 結ぶ in the standard expression for establishing an alliance.

1.13.n: Marks 同盟 as what the clans establish.

1.14.n: Polite form of 結ぶ; the present tense makes this historical narration feel immediate.

2.0.n: Points back to the alliance just described.

2.1.n: Marks これ as the thing being identified by the alliance's name.

2.3.n: In this alliance name, 甲 abbreviates Kai Province and 相 abbreviates Sagami Province.

2.4.n: This character abbreviates the province name Suruga within the alliance's name.

2.5.n: Here 国 refers to historical Japanese provinces, not modern countries.

2.6.n: This completes the historical alliance's name.

2.7.n: Politely identifies the alliance; Japanese uses present tense here even though the events are historical.

3.0.n: Connects the alliance arrangements to the cooperation that follows.

3.1.n: Used figuratively: entrusting your back to someone means relying on their protection.

3.2.n: Marks 背中 as what the clans entrust to one another.

3.3.n: 預ける combines with 合う to show that the clans perform the action mutually.

3.4.n: After a verb, 形 describes the way an action or situation takes shape.

3.5.n: With 形, marks the arrangement under which the clans expand.

4.0.n: 北条 is a clan name; 氏 here means clan, not the personal title Mr. or Ms.

4.1.n: Marks the Hojo as a topic contrasted with the other clans.

4.2.n: Names the direction of the Hojo clan's expansion.

4.3.n: Marks the direction of expansion and is pronounced え.

4.5.n: 武田 is a clan name, with 氏 identifying the clan as a whole.

4.6.n: Introduces the Takeda in parallel with the other two clans.

4.7.n: Names the direction of the Takeda clan's expansion.

4.8.n: Marks the direction of expansion; the shared verb comes at the sentence's end.

4.10.n: 今川 is a clan name, with 氏 identifying the clan as a whole.

4.11.n: Introduces the Imagawa as the last of the three contrasted topics.

4.12.n: Names the direction of the Imagawa clan's expansion.

4.13.n: Marks the direction in which the Imagawa extend their influence.

4.14.n: After the final へ, と rounds off the listed directions before the shared verb.

4.15.n: Refers to the clans' political and military reach.

4.16.n: Marks 勢力 as what the clans expand.

4.17.n: The て-form of 伸ばす plus いきます presents expansion as continuing onward; ます makes it polite.

0.lit: After that, as for the three clans of Takeda, Hojo, and Imagawa,
0.tip: The final は sets up a topic whose action is explained in the next line.

1.lit: By marrying off their respective daughters into the respective families, they form an alliance.
1.tip: A verb followed by ことで means by doing that action.

2.lit: This is the Kai–Sagami–Suruga three-province alliance.
2.tip: 甲相駿 compresses three province names into one character each.

3.lit: In this way, in an arrangement of entrusting their backs to one another,
3.tip: Adding 合う to a verb expresses doing something to or with one another.

4.lit: Hojo clan eastward, Takeda clan northward, Imagawa clan westward: they continue extending their influence.
4.tip: All three clan-and-direction phrases share the single verb at the end.
